meanings.usage: 指人或动物的骨骼框架，也可引申为不可告人的秘密
用来描述人或家庭品行端正、符合社会道德标准
及物动词，宾语可以是具体物品或抽象的信息、情绪等
常用来修饰描述、表达、记忆等，强调形象清晰鲜明
多用于描述事件、场景充满戏剧张力，有突然或惊人的效果
指公众对某人/机构的评价，常见搭配ruin/damage one's reputation
对应阳性形式hero，指故事、小说中的女主角或杰出女性
作及物动词时直接接被毒害的对象；也可作名词表示“毒药”
区别于非虚构作品（non-fiction），也可指不真实的事情
指将物品整齐堆叠，也可作名词表示“一堆（物品）”
形容人因极度恐惧而无法动弹的状态
指物体悬垂着来回摆动
可指物体缓慢摇摆，也可引申为“影响、说服某人”
强调动作幅度大且突然，常见搭配leap out at sb
sympathetic的反义词，指对他人的遭遇没有共情

phrases.usage: 固定习语，指家庭或个人不愿公开的丑事、家丑

examples.en: After the politician resigned, the public found he had many skeletons in the cupboard.
examples.zh: 这位政客辞职后，公众发现他有很多不可告人的丑事。

phrases.usage: 表示“在不同程度上”，用于说明事物的程度差异

examples.en: Students in this class are to varying degrees interested in art.
examples.zh: 这个班的学生对艺术的兴趣程度各不相同。

phrases.usage: 表示“为……感到骄傲/得意”，后接名词、代词或动名词

examples.en: She is very proud of her daughter's performance in the competition.
examples.zh: 她为女儿在比赛中的表现感到非常骄傲。

phrases.usage: 常用于故事开头，表示“从前；曾经”，也可口语中提及过去的经历

examples.en: Once upon a time, there lived an old fisherman by the sea.
examples.zh: 从前，海边住着一位老渔夫。

phrases.usage: 表示“带领某人到（某地）”，常用于接待客人的场景

examples.en: The waiter showed us to our table near the window.
examples.zh: 服务员把我们领到了靠窗的桌子旁。

phrases.usage: (毛发) 竖立，通常用来形容人非常恐惧、震惊

examples.en: The horror movie was so scary that it made my hair stand on end.
examples.zh: 这部恐怖电影太吓人了，吓得我汗毛都竖起来了。

phrases.usage: 表示“即将做某事；正要做某事”，强调动作马上就要发生

examples.en: I was about to go out when the phone rang.

phrases.usage: 表示“冲向；猛奔到某地”，强调动作的急促

examples.en: When the bell rang, he dashed to the classroom.
examples.zh: 铃声一响，他就冲向了教室。

sentences.en: We often read in novels how a seemingly respectable person
sentences.zh: 我们经常在小说中读到，一个看似体面的人

sentences.en: or family has some terrible secret which has been concealed from strangers for years.
sentences.zh: 或家庭隐藏着某个可怕的秘密，多年来一直对陌生人保密。

sentences.en: The English language possesses a vivid saying to describe this sort of situation.
sentences.zh: 英语中有一个生动的说法来描述这种情况。

sentences.en: The terrible secret is called 'a skeleton in the cupboard'.
sentences.zh: 这个可怕的秘密被称为“橱柜里的骷髅”。

sentences.en: At some dramatic moment in the story, the terrible secret becomes known and a reputation is ruined.
sentences.zh: 在故事的某个戏剧性时刻，这个可怕的秘密公诸于世，声誉也随之毁掉。

sentences.en: The reader's hair stands on end when he reads in the final pages of the novel that the heroine,
sentences.zh: 当读者在小说的最后几页读到女主人公——

sentences.en: a dear old lady who had always been so kind to everybody, had, in her youth, poisoned every one of her five husbands.
sentences.zh: 一位一直对每个人都非常和蔼可亲的老太太，在年轻时毒死了她的五个丈夫时，会毛骨悚然。

sentences.en: It is all very well for such things to occur in fiction.
sentences.zh: 这种事情发生在小说里是完全可以的。

sentences.en: To varying degrees, we all have secrets which we do not want even our closest friends to learn,
sentences.zh: 在不同程度上，我们都有一些甚至不想让最亲密的朋友知道的秘密，

sentences.en: but few of us have skeletons in the cupboard.
sentences.zh: 但我们中很少有人有“橱柜里的骷髅”。

sentences.en: The only person I know who has a skeleton in the cupboard is George Carlton, and he is very proud of the fact.
sentences.zh: 我认识的唯一一个有“橱柜里的骷髅”的人是乔治·卡尔顿，他对此引以为豪。

sentences.en: George studied medicine in his youth.
sentences.zh: 乔治年轻时学医。

sentences.en: Instead of becoming a doctor, however, he became a successful writer of detective stories.
sentences.zh: 然而，他没有成为一名医生，而是成为了一名成功的侦探小说作家。

sentences.en: I once spent an uncomfortable weekend which I shall never forget at his house.
sentences.zh: 我有一次在他家度过了一个令我永生难忘的不舒服的周末。

sentences.en: George showed me to the guestroom which, he said, was rarely used.
sentences.zh: 乔治把我带到客房，他说那个房间很少用。

sentences.en: He told me to unpack my things and then come down to dinner.
sentences.zh: 他让我把行李打开，然后下来吃饭。

sentences.en: After I had stacked my shirts and underclothes in two empty drawers, I decided to hang one of the two suits I had brought with me in the cupboard.
sentences.zh: 我把衬衫和内衣叠放在两个空抽屉里后，决定把我带来的两套西装中的一套挂在橱柜里。

sentences.en: I opened the cupboard door and then stood in front of it petrified.
sentences.zh: 我打开橱柜门，然后僵在原地，吓呆了。

sentences.en: A skeleton was dangling before my eyes.
sentences.zh: 一个骷髅在我眼前晃动。

sentences.en: The sudden movement of the door made it sway slightly and it gave me the impression that it was about to leap out at me.
sentences.zh: 门的突然移动使它轻轻摇晃，给我一种它要向我扑过来的感觉。

sentences.en: Dropping my suit, I dashed downstairs to tell George.
sentences.zh: 我扔下西装，冲下楼去告诉乔治。

sentences.en: This was worse than 'a terrible secret'; this was a real skeleton!
sentences.zh: 这比“可怕的秘密”更糟糕；这是一个真正的骷髅！

sentences.en: But George was unsympathetic.
sentences.zh: 但乔治无动于衷。

sentences.en: 'Oh, that,' he said with a smile as if he were talking about an old friend.
sentences.zh: “哦，那个啊，”他微笑着说，好像在谈论一位老朋友。

sentences.en: 'That's Sebastian. You forget that I was a medical student once upon a time.'
sentences.zh: “那是塞巴斯蒂安。你忘了我以前也是个医学院的学生。”

exercises.prompt: “在复合句中修饰名词或代词的从句，被修饰的词叫先行词，从句由关系代词或关系副词引导” 描述的是哪个语法点？
exercises.hint: 先行词 + 关系代词/副词 + 从句其余部分
options: Not only...but (also) 引起的倒装句
定语从句中的“介词+which”结构
exercises.explain: 定语从句：先行词 + 关系代词/副词 + 从句其余部分：用来对先行词进行补充说明，若从句是限定性的则无需逗号分隔，非限定性的需用逗号和主句隔开

exercises.prompt:
选出下面句子的正确中文意思：

options: 下面这个“病态幽默”的例子能让你自己评判。
我打开橱柜门，然后僵在原地，吓呆了。
在20世纪80年代初，电脑巨头IBM生产了世界上第一台个人电脑。

grammar.title: 定语从句
grammar.definition: 在复合句中修饰名词或代词的从句，被修饰的词叫先行词，从句由关系代词或关系副词引导
grammar.structure: 先行词 + 关系代词/副词 + 从句其余部分
grammar.usage: 用来对先行词进行补充说明，若从句是限定性的则无需逗号分隔，非限定性的需用逗号和主句隔开

examples.en: The only person I know who has a skeleton in the cupboard is George Carlton.
examples.zh: 我认识的人中唯一有“家丑”的是乔治·卡尔顿。

examples.en: The old lady who had always been so kind to everybody poisoned her husbands.
examples.zh: 那位一直对所有人都很和善的老妇人毒死了她的丈夫们。

grammar.title: as if 引导的方式状语从句
grammar.definition: 用来引导表示“好像、似乎”的从句，描述动作的方式，可接真实情况或虚拟情况
grammar.structure: 主句 + as if + 从句
grammar.usage: 当描述的内容是非真实的、与事实相反的情况时，从句要用虚拟语气；若表示可能真实的情况则用陈述语气

examples.en: He said with a smile as if he were talking about an old friend.
examples.zh: 他笑着说，好像在谈论一位老朋友似的。

examples.en: It looks as if it is going to rain soon.
examples.zh: 看起来好像马上就要下雨了。

patterns.pattern: It is all very well for sth to occur...

original.en: It is all very well for such things to occur in fiction.
original.zh: 这种事发生在小说里是无可厚非的。

examples.en: It is all very well for jokes to appear in comedy shows.
examples.zh: 这种笑话出现在喜剧节目里是无可厚非的。

examples.en: It is all very well for kids to make small mistakes.
examples.zh: 小孩子犯点小错是很正常的。

patterns.pattern: The only person I know who... is...

original.en: The only person I know who has a skeleton in the cupboard is George Carlton.
original.zh: 我认识的人中唯一有“家丑”的是乔治·卡尔顿。

examples.en: The only person I know who can play the violin well is my deskmate.
examples.zh: 我认识的人里唯一小提琴拉得好的是我的同桌。

examples.en: The only restaurant I know which serves authentic Sichuan food is near the station.
examples.zh: 我知道的唯一一家做正宗川菜的餐馆在车站附近。

patterns.pattern: It gave me the impression that...

original.en: It gave me the impression that it was about to leap out at me.
original.zh: 它给我的感觉是好像就要扑到我身上来了。

examples.en: His polite words gave me the impression that he was a very well-educated person.
examples.zh: 他礼貌的话语给我的印象是他是个很有教养的人。

examples.en: The quiet town gave me the impression that time had slowed down here.
examples.zh: 这个安静的小镇给我的感觉是时间在这里都变慢了。
